title: Cash deposits split across branches of the same institution
definition: Cash deposits made at different branches of the same institution within a short window, in amounts that would have been reportable had they been made in one transaction. The indicator measures the dispersion of deposits across a single institution's network; it does not establish that a reporting requirement was avoided, because branch dispersion has operational explanations.
evidence_to_cite: the deposit records, each cited by its own source id and pointer
the branch identifiers and the aggregation rule applied for the date
the customer's stated reason for depositing at more than one branch, where recorded
benign_explanations: A customer who works near one branch and lives near another.
A business with several sites that deposits each site's takings at its local branch.
A customer avoiding a branch queue or a daily branch limit.
An automated cash-handling arrangement between a business and its branches.

sources.citation: Financial Crimes Enforcement Network, currency transaction reporting and the aggregation rule, summarised in the FinCrime regulatory index.
